definitions.definition: u_tt(x,t)=∂u_t(x,t)/∂t, the componentwise second time derivative.

definitions.type: spatial derivative matrix field on ℝ^n × (0,∞)
definitions.definition: D_xu has columns ∂_{x_j}u for j=1,...,n, with ∂_{x_j} the componentwise partial derivative in coordinate j; ∂_{x_jx_j}u denotes its second derivative in that coordinate. Derivatives of u_t use the same convention. Its Frobenius square is |D_xu|²=Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|².

e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². Norms and dot products throughout are Euclidean; all spatial integrals are Lebesgue integrals, written dx. Write e_t for the time partial derivative of e.
E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n}e(x,t) dx, the finite real Lebesgue integral, with exactly the normalization in the exercise (no factor 1/2).

inputs.statement: u:ℝ^n × (0,∞) → ℝ^m is jointly C^∞ (smooth) on this open domain.

For every x∈ℝ^n and t>0, u(x,t)·u_t(x,t)=0 and u_t(x,t)·(u_tt(x,t)−Δ_xu(x,t))=0. Moreover every scalar a satisfying u_tt(x,t)−Δ_xu(x,t)=a u(x,t) equals Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|²−|u_t(x,t)|²; consequently u_tt−Δ_xu=(Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|²)u pointwise.

inputs.statement: For every t0>0, let J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. There exist a compact C⊂ℝ^n and R>0 such that C⊂(−R,R)^n and u(x,r)=q for x∉C and r∈J. Put Q=[−R,R]^n; Q has finite Lebesgue measure (2R)^n. All positive-order derivatives of u vanish on (ℝ^n∖C)×int J. For every r∈int J, each of e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t(·,r)·u_tt(·,r), and, for j=1,...,n, ∂_{x_j}u(·,r)·∂_{x_j}u_t(·,r), u_t(·,r)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(·,r), and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u)(·,r) is continuous, zero outside C, bounded on Q and absolutely Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n. In particular e(·,t) is integrable for every t>0. The fields e and e_t are jointly continuous on ℝ^n×(0,∞).

argument.text: Fix t0>0. N002 proves integrability of e(·,t0) and of all product terms below, so E is the actual finite integral. N003 proves its differentiability and gives E'(t0)=∫e_t(x,t0) dx with e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_{j=1}^n∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t. Substitute this identity, use linearity and interchange the finite sum and integral (H001 gives a finite dimension), and apply N004 to each j. This yields E'(t0)=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·u_tt dx−2Σ_{j=1}^n∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u dx=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu) dx, all fields evaluated at t0.

produces.statement: E is differentiable at t0 and E'(t0)=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·(u_tt(x,t0)−Δ_xu(x,t0)) dx.

argument.text: By N001 the final integrand in F001 is zero at every x, so E'(t0)=0. Since t0 was arbitrary, N002 and N003 together prove the complete target: e(·,t) is integrable and E is differentiable with E'(t)=0 for every positive t. No time-zero value or limiting assertion is used.

produces.statement: For every r>0, e(·,r) is integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

argument.text: To retain the final conservation statement of the supplied proof, fix s,t>0. If s<t, apply M004 to E and the zero derivative on [s,t]; extend E by zero to nonpositive times solely to match the source's total domain. F002 gives differentiability and hence continuity at all points of this positive closed interval, and derivative zero in its interior. The theorem gives slope zero and therefore E(t)=E(s). If t<s use the same application with the endpoints interchanged, and if s=t equality is immediate. Thus E is constant on (0,∞). This retains exactly the exercise's normalization.
